meta.title: JOURNEYWAYS | The Digital Game
meta.description: The JOURNEYWAYS digital version, in active development at v0.7.0-alpha. Real-time multiplayer, trilingual interface (English, Spanish, French), privacy by design (no camera), web-based with no install required. Master's research at UBC GRSJ.

hero.title: The digital version.
hero.tagline: Same game. Web-native. Built in the open.
hero.lead: JOURNEYWAYS is being built as a digital game in parallel with the board game. Same design philosophy, same five card categories, same modular map, same private journal. Different medium, same commitment to identity exploration and collaborative narrative.

spec.note: Repository is private during development. Open to the public at release.

premise.p1: The digital version exists to remove barriers, not to replace the table. Players can participate from anywhere; sessions span geographies; there is no camera support so the focus stays on words and stories. Solo and group play, real-time multiplayer, trilingual at launch.
premise.p2: The repository is private during development; access by request. It will be made public when the project is released.

built.intro: Shipped in the current alpha build.

multiplayer.title: Real-time multiplayer
multiplayer.body: Lobby, dashboard, and play view show who is present. Collaborative canvas synchronization keeps everyone's view in step.

cards.title: Five-color card system
cards.body: The same map-tile and card-pile system as the board game, recreated as an interactive canvas. Red Encounters, Green Movement, Blue Reflections, Black Countdown, Purple Group actions. Browse the decks.

table.title: The shared game table
table.body: Every card is shuffled together and dealt into a handful of uneven, face-down piles around a shared table, each showing its suit on the back; the map tiles stack the same way on their wooden backs. Pick the top of a pile and it turns face up for the whole room to look at, then place it on the table wherever you like. A game's organizer can set how many Countdown cards are in play and reshuffle the deck mid-game, with every traveller asked to agree first.

journal.title: Private journal with sketch preview
journal.body: Per-player journal: write entries, sketch with the canvas tool, browse previous entries with thumbnail previews.

origins.title: Character origins as PDF
origins.body: Players can export their character creation page as a US Letter PDF for printing or archival.

trilingual.title: Trilingual interface
trilingual.body: English, Spanish, and French at launch. User-created content stays in the language the user wrote it; nothing gets auto-translated.

privacy.title: Privacy by design
privacy.body: No camera support. Argon2id password hashing, Cloudflare Turnstile verification, journals scoped per session. All data hosted in Canada.

recent.body: The full development log now lives on the Updates page, alongside the board game's milestones.

print.title: Printable cards, tiles, and booklets
print.body: A single typesetting pipeline that turns the catalogue into print-ready files: the full card and map-tile sets, the player booklet, and the user manual, all generated from the same source as the screen versions so they never drift apart. Coming very soon.

story_loop.title: Story loop
story_loop.body: The shared table is in place; next is the full journaling turn that builds on it: pick a card from a chosen suit, write a short entry from it, and share it with the room.

chat.title: In-room chat
chat.body: Plain text chat inside your room, alongside the canvas and the journal. Voice and video stay outside the application; bring your own.

export.title: Take your stories with you
export.body: Export your character data, narrative entries, and reflections in a portable format you can keep, even after the session ends.

mobile.title: Mobile responsiveness
mobile.body: Phones are advisory for now. Full small-screen support is planned.

docs.title: Open documentation
docs.body: The full project, in plain technical writing, visible on the site: security, privacy, data governance, infrastructure. For anyone who wants to look under the hood.

beta.title: Quiet beta, then larger sessions
beta.body: First closed beta with a small group, then larger play sessions. No launch campaign; updates here as they happen.

hybrid.title: Hybrid play (longer-term)
hybrid.body: A mixed-medium variant that combines physical components, like the player booklet, with digital ones, like the board map.
